description: Main Stage presentations at DEF CON 30 covering cutting-edge hardware hacking, cloud security, binary exploitation, automotive systems, cryptography, satellite communications, and cyber policy.

talks.title: Welcome to DEF CON & The Making of the DEF CON 30 Badge
talks.teaser: The Dark Tangent and MK Factor welcome hackers to DEF CON 30 and reveal the design, musical synthesis hardware, and puzzles behind the DC30 badge.
talks.summary:
In the opening ceremonies of DEF CON 30 on the Main Stage, conference founder The Dark Tangent (Jeff Moss) welcomes thousands of hackers to celebrate the landmark 30th anniversary of the convention. At 07:05, MK Factor (Michael Katie) takes the stage to present the highly anticipated annual Badge Talk, detailing the engineering, art, and manufacturing behind the DEF CON 30 electronic badge.

The speakers dive into the badge's aesthetic design at 14:00, exploring how custom multi-layer silk-screen artwork and retro hacker iconography were blended across the hardware. At 21:00, they detail the physical hardware architecture—a dual-board PCB sandwich equipped with mechanical keyboard switches, interactive LEDs, and precision circuit assembly handled by partner PCBX.

At 28:00, MK Factor demonstrates the badge's firmware capabilities, highlighting polyphonic audio synthesis, custom musical tones, and interactive puzzle modes. At 35:00, the presenters share the monumental logistical challenges overcome during production, including global semiconductor shortages and supply chain disruptions. The session closes at 41:00 with audience questions regarding Easter eggs and hardware hacking add-ons. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Hacking the Farm: Breaking Badly into Agricultural Devices
talks.teaser: Sick Codes demonstrates tractor-sized hardware hacking on John Deere display consoles, extracting firmware, bypassing locks, and running Doom on farm machinery.
talks.summary:
The Right to Repair and Agricultural Equipment Security

Modern agricultural machinery relies heavily on proprietary embedded electronic control units and telematics displays that lock farmers out of self-repair and diagnostic workflows.

Hardware Hacking John Deere Touchscreen Consoles

Sick Codes demonstrates physical hardware attack vectors on John Deere display terminals—including glitching, desoldering flash memory, and extracting embedded Linux filesystems.

Duplicating, Emulating, and Modifying Farm Firmware

The author shows how extracted firmware images can be modified, re-flashed, and emulated in QEMU to bypass digital rights management and diagnostic restrictions.

Advancing Agricultural Right-to-Repair Legislation

The presentation emphasizes the critical intersection between firmware security research, food supply resilience, and legislative right-to-repair initiatives.

talks.title: Solana JIT: Lessons from Fuzzing a Smart Contract Compiler
talks.teaser: Thomas Roth (stacksmashing) shares insights from fuzzing the Solana eBPF Just-In-Time (JIT) smart contract compiler, uncovering critical consensus-breaking bugs.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Blockchain JIT Compilers

High-performance blockchain platforms rely on Just-In-Time (JIT) compilers to execute eBPF smart contracts rapidly; however, compiler bugs can lead to consensus divergence or node crashes.

Understanding Solana's rbpf Architecture

Thomas Roth analyzes Solana's eBPF virtual machine and JIT compiler implementation (rbpf), dissecting how bytecode translates to native x86 machine instructions.

Building Specialized Differential JIT Fuzzers

Roth details developing differential fuzzing harnesses that execute randomized eBPF instructions simultaneously across the JIT engine and software interpreter to flag discrepancies.

Securing Core Blockchain Infrastructure

The author reviews discovered compiler bugs, discusses responsible vulnerability disclosure with the Solana team, and outlines fuzzing best practices for smart contract virtual machines.

talks.title: Contests Closing Ceremonies & Awards
talks.teaser: The official DEF CON 30 contest closing ceremonies celebrate the winners and record-breaking achievements across all conference contests and challenges.
talks.summary:
The DEF CON 30 Contests Closing Ceremonies celebrate the champions, participants, and volunteer organizers across the wide spectrum of official DEF CON competitions.

[24:02] Ceremony hosts review the creative and technical achievements across community contests, highlighting standout entries from the Tin Foil Hat contest, the legendary Hacker Jeopardy tournament [36:00], physical lockpicking championships, wireless Fox and Hound hunts, and social engineering challenges.

[47:25] The ceremony culminates in the presentation of the coveted DEF CON Black Badges—the highest honor awarded to winners of premier competitions, granting them free lifetime entry to DEF CON. Organizers commend the community's collaborative spirit, problem-solving skills, and dedication to pushing the boundaries of security research [58:37].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Closing Ceremonies & Awards
talks.teaser: The concluding closing ceremonies for DEF CON 30, celebrating community accomplishments, contest winners, and conference wrap-up announcements.
talks.summary:
DEF CON Conference Presentation

This segment features remarks and presentations from DEF CON organizers and security leaders. Topics include the state of cybersecurity, hacker culture, community initiatives, and the conference's impact on the security landscape.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: The Journey From Isolated Container to Cluster Admin
talks.teaser: Aviv Sasson details discovering FabricEscape, a severe vulnerability in Microsoft Service Fabric allowing unprivileged containers to seize full cluster admin rights.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Microsoft Service Fabric

Microsoft Service Fabric is an enterprise-grade distributed systems platform and container orchestrator powering critical Microsoft Azure cloud infrastructure and internal services.

Discovering the FabricEscape Container Escape Vulnerability

Aviv Sasson dissects the FabricLifecycleWorkflowManager component, identifying race conditions and unvalidated path traversals in container deployment processes.

Escalating from Container to Full Host and Node Admin

Sasson demonstrates weaponizing the flaw to break out of Linux container sandboxes, execute code on host nodes, and harvest cluster management certificates.

Remediation and Cloud Multi-Tenant Hardening

The author discusses Microsoft's coordinated patch deployment (CVE-2022-30137) and strategies for hardening multi-tenant container orchestration architectures.

talks.title: Save Environment Variable: Hijacking Legit Apps with Minimal Footprint
talks.teaser: Wietze Beukema presents novel DLL hijacking techniques that manipulate user-controlled environment variables to execute code via signed binaries with zero file drops.
talks.summary:
The Maturation of Classic DLL Hijacking Defenses

Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions have extensively mapped standard DLL search order hijacking, making traditional binary planting detectable.

Discovering Environment Variable DLL Dependencies

Wietze Beukema investigates how legitimate, digitally signed Windows executables expand user-controllable environment variables to resolve dependency paths.

Executing Payloads with Minimal Forensics Footprints

Beukema demonstrates setting arbitrary environment variables to steer trusted system binaries into loading malicious DLLs from atypical locations without modifying system files.

Detection Strategies for Hunting Anomalous DLL Loads

The author provides incident responders with Sigma detection rules and telemetry queries to detect suspicious environment variable manipulations.

talks.title: Bypassing Android Permissions from All Protection Levels
talks.teaser: Nikita Kurtin uncovers universal Android permission bypass vulnerabilities affecting over 98% of active devices, subverting signature and privileged protection levels.
talks.summary:
The Android Permission Architecture and Protection Levels

Android's security model relies on permission levels—normal, dangerous, signature, and privileged—to restrict access to sensitive device APIs, hardware, and user data.

Analyzing IPC Flaws and Binder Proxy Confusion

Nikita Kurtin explores inter-process communication (IPC) vulnerabilities in system services, demonstrating how unprivileged apps confuse Binder proxy identity tokens.

Bypassing Signature-Level Permissions Across Android Releases

Kurtin demonstrates step-by-step exploit chains that allow untrusted third-party apps to access location, camera, and system settings without user consent.

Platform Hardening and IPC Validation in AOSP

The author reviews Google's upstream Android Open Source Project (AOSP) patches and provides mobile developers with secure Binder verification patterns.

talks.title: ClickOnce AbUse for Trusted Code Execution
talks.teaser: Nick Powers and Steven Flores show how Microsoft ClickOnce technology can be abused for stealthy phishing initial access, bypassing Mark-of-the-Web and AppLocker.
talks.summary:
The Erosion of Traditional Phishing Initial Access Payloads

With Microsoft disabling Office macros by default and Mark-of-the-Web (MOTW) protections expanding, red teams need alternative initial access vectors.

Deconstructing Microsoft ClickOnce Architecture

Nick Powers and Steven Flores analyze ClickOnce, a native Windows deployment technology designed to launch smart client applications directly from web links.

Weaponizing ClickOnce for Code Execution and Persistence

The speakers demonstrate crafting benign-looking ClickOnce deployment manifests that execute arbitrary .NET binaries while evading browser and endpoint security controls.

Defending Enterprise Environments Against ClickOnce Abuse

The authors provide enterprise defenders with group policy configurations, AppLocker rules, and telemetry monitoring to block unauthorized ClickOnce execution.

talks.title: Taking a Dump in the Cloud: Extracting Secrets from Office Integration
talks.teaser: Melvin Langvik reverses Microsoft Office desktop cloud integration, demonstrating how attackers extract cached OAuth tokens, PRTs, and cloud credentials from memory.
talks.summary:
The Convergence of Desktop Applications and Cloud Services

Modern Microsoft Office desktop applications maintain continuous, seamless authenticated sessions with Azure AD, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

Reverse Engineering Office Authentication Internals

Melvin Langvik investigates the undocumented IPC mechanisms and memory structures used by desktop Office binaries to interact with the Web Account Manager (WAM).

Harvesting Primary Refresh Tokens and OAuth Secrets

Langvik demonstrates dumping unencrypted cloud access tokens, refresh tokens, and session credentials directly from unprivileged user processes.

Threat Hunting and Token Protection Mitigations

The author provides defensive teams with behavioral detection patterns and discusses hardware-backed token binding implementations to stop token replay attacks.

talks.title: Pre-Auth RCE Chains on an MDM: Exploiting Quest KACE SMA
talks.teaser: Jeffrey Hofmann details discovering multiple pre-authentication remote code execution chains in Quest KACE Systems Management Appliance (SMA).
talks.summary:
Mobile Device Management (MDM) as Single Points of Failure

Centralized endpoint management appliances maintain privileged administrative agents across an entire enterprise fleet, making them prime targets for initial access.

Auditing the Quest KACE SMA Web Interface

Jeffrey Hofmann details reverse engineering the KACE SMA firmware, discovering authentication bypasses and unauthenticated SQL injection flaws.

Chaining Vulnerabilities into Root Remote Code Execution

Hofmann demonstrates chaining unauthenticated API endpoints with command injection in backend PHP handlers to achieve instant root-level shell access.

Vendor Remediation and Enterprise MDM Hardening

The author outlines the coordinated vulnerability disclosure timeline and offers hardening advice for isolating management appliances behind VPN perimeters.

talks.title: The Call is Coming from Inside the Cluster: Kubernetes Third-Party Tool Risks
talks.teaser: Dagan Henderson and Will Kline audit popular Kubernetes add-ons, exposing how third-party storage, logging, and observability tools introduce cluster takeover paths.
talks.summary:
The Expanding Ecosystem of Kubernetes Add-Ons

While Kubernetes core components have undergone intensive security audits, popular third-party operators, CSI drivers, and monitoring agents remain highly vulnerable.

Auditing Third-Party Helm Charts and CRDs

Dagan Henderson and Will Kline evaluate prevalent open-source Kubernetes utilities, revealing excessive RBAC permissions and unauthenticated metrics endpoints.

Exploiting Internal Add-Ons for Cluster Takeover

The speakers demonstrate how compromising a low-privilege add-on container enables escalating privileges to cluster-admin via exposed service account tokens.

Securing the Kubernetes Supply Chain

The authors present auditing toolchains, least-privilege RBAC templates, and admission controller policies to prevent lateral movement across cluster workloads.

talks.title: Emulation-Driven Reverse Engineering for Finding Vulnerabilities
talks.teaser: Security researcher atlas demonstrates partial CPU emulation with Unicorn Engine, bypassing tedious static assembly analysis to rapidly discover vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
The Cognitive Overload of Manual Reverse Engineering

Dissecting thousands of lines of complex disassembled assembly or decompiled C code is mentally exhausting and prone to human oversight.

Introducing Partial Emulation with Unicorn Engine

Atlas demonstrates setting up lightweight CPU emulation harnesses to execute isolated binary functions without needing a full system environment.

Automating State Inspection and Taint Tracking

The speaker shows how partial emulation allows dynamic memory tracing, register state inspection, and automated input mutation directly inside target routines.

Accelerating Vulnerability Discovery Workflows

The presentation provides open-source Python scripts and practical examples of discovering buffer overflows and logic bugs in proprietary binaries.

talks.title: ElectroVolt: Pwning Popular Desktop Apps via Electron Framework Flaws
talks.teaser: Aaditya Purani and Max Garrett expose systemic Electron framework misconfigurations, turning standard web XSS into remote code execution across popular desktop apps.
talks.summary:
The Ubiquity of Electron Desktop Applications

Leading enterprise collaboration, developer tools, and consumer messaging apps rely on Electron to package Chromium and Node.js into standalone cross-platform software.

Analyzing Node Integration and Context Isolation

Aaditya Purani and Max Garrett dissect recurring developer misconfigurations—including disabled context isolation, insecure preload scripts, and custom IPC handlers.

Weaponizing Remote Content for Code Execution

The authors demonstrate chaining cross-site scripting (XSS) in loaded web views to execute arbitrary system shell commands on macOS and Windows hosts.

Hardening Guidelines for Electron Developers

The presentation provides a comprehensive security checklist—enforcing strict Content Security Policies (CSP), secure IPC design, and context bridge validation.

talks.title: Crossing the KASM: A Web Application Pentest Story
talks.teaser: Samuel Erb and Justin Gardner share the story of finding and exploiting a complex RCE exploit chain against KASM Workspaces streaming software.
talks.summary:
Auditing Containerized Virtual Workspaces

KASM Workspaces provides enterprise streaming of isolated virtual desktop containers to deliver browser-based workspaces to corporate users.

Deconstructing KASM Web Management Architecture

Samuel Erb and Justin Gardner analyze the multi-tiered architecture of KASM, identifying subtle flaws in session token handling and websocket routing.

Chaining Web Vulnerabilities to Container Compromise

The speakers walk through an ingenious exploit chain combining parameter injection, token manipulation, and API bypasses to achieve remote code execution.

Coordinated Disclosure and Hardening Lessons

The authors discuss working with KASM developers to patch the vulnerability and share takeaways for auditing container streaming platforms.

talks.title: Low Code, High Risk: Enterprise Domination via Low-Code Abuse
talks.teaser: Michael Bargury explores enterprise domination through low-code shadow IT, abusing Microsoft Power Platform connectors and flows to exfiltrate corporate data.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Low-Code and Citizen Developers

Enterprises increasingly encourage non-technical employees to build automated business workflows using low-code platforms like Microsoft Power Apps and Power Automate.

Analyzing Low-Code Shadow IT Attack Surfaces

Michael Bargury demonstrates how unmonitored user flows inherit broad enterprise API permissions, connecting SQL databases, email systems, and cloud storage.

Abusing Connectors for Covert Data Exfiltration and Escalation

Bargury showcases techniques for creating malicious connectors, exfiltrating sensitive tenant data, and establishing persistent administrative backdoors.

Enterprise Governance and Low-Code Security Tooling

The author provides security architects with Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy templates, tenant isolation rules, and automated auditing scripts.

talks.title: Digital Skeleton Keys: Spoofing Offline RFID Access Control Systems
talks.teaser: Miana Windall and Micsen investigate offline RFID access control systems, demonstrating how to forge cryptographic card data to create universal digital skeleton keys.
talks.summary:
The Trust Architecture of Offline RFID Locks

Offline electronic locks do not maintain real-time network connectivity, relying entirely on the cryptographic data stored inside RFID keycards to make access decisions.

Reverse Engineering Offline Card Formats

Miana Windall and Micsen dissect proprietary card data structures, discovering replay weaknesses, weak cryptographic keys, and unauthenticated sector data.

Forging Master Key Credentials and Time Stamps

The speakers demonstrate modifying expiration timestamps, room permissions, and site codes to forge functioning master digital skeleton keys on blank Mifare cards.

Remediation for Facility Managers and Manufacturers

The authors recommend modern cryptographic lock architectures, rolling dynamic challenge-response protocols, and regular key blacklist updates.

talks.title: Internet Server Error: Exploiting Interprocess Communication in Embedded HTTP
talks.teaser: Martin Doyhenard demonstrates reverse engineering proprietary HTTP servers, exploiting interprocess communication (IPC) and memory corruption for remote code execution.
talks.summary:
The Fragile Nature of Proprietary Embedded Web Servers

Many commercial networking and IoT devices utilize custom, closed-source HTTP server daemons to manage user requests and interface with backend system services.

Reverse Engineering Custom HTTP Parsers and IPC Handlers

Martin Doyhenard details dissecting proprietary binaries in IDA Pro, identifying flaws in request parsing, header extraction, and shared memory IPC messaging.

Exploiting Memory Corruption via HTTP Request Smuggling

Doyhenard demonstrates chaining HTTP request manipulation with heap buffer overflows to achieve reliable remote code execution on target appliances.

Defensive Architecture and Memory-Safe Migration

The author highlights the critical need for memory-safe languages and standard open-source web daemons in embedded firmware design.

talks.title: CSRF Resurrections: Starring the Unholy Trinity
talks.teaser: Dongsung Kim demonstrates how modern browser features and emerging Web APIs can be chained to resurrect Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) despite SameSite cookies.
talks.summary:
The Premature Declaration of CSRF's Death

With browsers enforcing SameSite=Lax cookie policies by default, many developers assume that Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) has been completely eradicated.

Uncovering SameSite Bypass Vectors

Dongsung Kim analyzes subtle browser behavior quirks, top-level navigation exceptions, and client-side redirects that allow attackers to bypass Lax restrictions.

Chaining the Unholy Trinity of Web Features

Kim demonstrates chaining window opening methods, service worker caches, and navigation timing bugs to reliably execute authenticated state-changing requests.

Robust Defensive Standards for Modern Web Apps

The presentation emphasizes why defense-in-depth—including custom header validation, explicit anti-CSRF tokens, and SameSite=Strict—remains indispensable.

talks.title: Defeating Moving Elements in High Security Keys
talks.teaser: Bill Graydon analyzes high-security lock designs featuring moving key elements, demonstrating bypasses, casting tricks, and 3D printing duplication techniques.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Moving Elements in High-Security Locks

To prevent unauthorized 3D printing and casting duplication, high-security lock manufacturers (Mul-T-Lock Interactive, EVVA, ASSA) introduced active moving elements on key blades.

Mechanical Internals of Active Key Mechanisms

Bill Graydon breaks down the physical mechanics of interactive spring-loaded balls, floating pins, and magnetic rotors inside keyways.

Duplicating and Defeating Moving Elements

Graydon showcases innovative duplication methods—including multi-part 3D resin printing, modular key blanks, and custom mechanical picking tools.

Implications for Commercial Physical Security

The author provides facility managers and security professionals with objective criteria for evaluating high-security mechanical access systems.

talks.title: Top Performing Account Crackers: Business Modules, Architecture, & Techniques
talks.teaser: Arik Atar dissects the commercial ecosystem of credential stuffing and bot networks, reverse engineering account crackers and automated scalp bots.
talks.summary:
The Lucrative Underground Industry of Automated Scalping

From high-demand electronics and limited sneakers to concert tickets, automated botnets monopolize online checkouts and execute massive credential stuffing campaigns.

Architecture and Business Models of Account Crackers

Arik Atar reverse engineers popular commercial cracking suites (SilverBullet, OpenBullet), examining proxy rotators, request solving engines, and fingerprint spoofers.

Bypassing Modern Bot Detection and CAPTCHAs

Atar illustrates how bot operators defeat behavioral telemetry, solve advanced CAPTCHAs via third-party farms, and mimic legitimate mobile browser signatures.

Enterprise Bot Mitigation and Adaptive Defenses

The presentation details effective defensive counter-strategies—including device attestation, behavioral rate limiting, and risk-based multi-factor authentication.

talks.title: Exploitation in the Era of Formal Verification
talks.teaser: Adam Zabrocki and Alex Tereshkin examine software exploitation in formally verified systems, identifying design flaws and specification gaps that bypass proofs.
talks.summary:
The Promise and Reality of Formal Software Verification

Formal verification mathematically proves that a software implementation adheres strictly to a specified formal model, aiming to eliminate entire classes of implementation bugs.

Analyzing Specification Gaps and Unverified Assumptions

Adam Zabrocki and Alex Tereshkin explore how subtle discrepancies between formal specifications and real-world hardware execution create exploitable attack vectors.

Developing Exploits Against Formally Verified Codebases

The authors demonstrate weaponizing memory corruption, timing side channels, and hardware fault injection against verified cryptographic routines and hypervisors.

Refining Formal Models for Real-World Security

The presentation offers recommendations for aligning mathematical security models with actual physical hardware execution constraints.

talks.title: Tor & Darknet OPSEC: Lessons from a Veteran Darknet Vendor
talks.teaser: Veteran darknet vendor Sam Bent shares real-world operational security lessons, dissecting common OPSEC failures, Bitcoin tracking, and digital hygiene.
talks.summary:
The Real-World Culture and Risks of Darknet Marketplaces

Operating within darknet economies requires an uncompromising approach to operational security, where a single operational mistake can lead to total deanonymization and arrest.

Deconstructing Critical OPSEC Failures

Sam Bent analyzes high-profile law enforcement takedowns, highlighting how stylistic writing analysis, metadata leaks, and payment reuse compromise hidden vendors.

Operational Hygiene for Tor, PGP, and Cryptocurrencies

Bent outlines rigorous daily operational protocols—including ephemeral Tails OS environments, strict PGP airgapping, and privacy-focused Monero transaction routing.

Essential Lessons for Privacy Advocates and Security Researchers

The author provides actionable privacy guidelines for threat researchers, journalists, and activists operating in hostile threat environments.

talks.title: Digging into Xiaomi's TEE to Get to Chinese Money
talks.teaser: Slava Makkaveev reverse engineers Xiaomi's Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), discovering critical vulnerabilities that allow forging mobile payment transactions.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Mobile Payment Trust in Asia

Mobile wallets process trillions of dollars annually, relying on the hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) to manage cryptographic keys and sign transactions.

Reverse Engineering Xiaomi's MediaTek TrustZone Architecture

Slava Makkaveev dissects Xiaomi's proprietary TEE microkernel, trustlets, and trusted application communication interfaces.

Discovering Memory Corruption in Payment Trustlets

Makkaveev details uncovering memory corruption vulnerabilities in WeChat Pay and Alipay trustlet binaries, enabling arbitrary code execution in secure world.

Forging Mobile Payment Signatures and Vendor Remediation

The author demonstrates extracting root payment signing keys to forge valid financial transactions and discusses Xiaomi's patch deployment.

talks.title: Perimeter Breached: Hacking a Network-Connected Access Control System
talks.teaser: Sam Quinn and Steve Povolny analyze building access control hardware, uncovering vulnerabilities in Mercury controllers that allow remote physical door unlocking.
talks.summary:
The Convergence of Physical and Network Security Perimeters

Enterprise physical access control systems (PACS) increasingly connect directly to IP networks, creating potential bridges between digital vulnerabilities and physical facility access.

Reverse Engineering Mercury Security Access Controllers

Sam Quinn and Steve Povolny audit Mercury EP-series controllers, discovering unauthenticated command execution and hardcoded cryptographic keys in backend daemons.

Remotely Unlocking Doors and Spoofing Badge Scans

The researchers demonstrate weaponizing discovered flaws over the network to instantly trigger door strikes, unlock secured zones, and forge audit logs.

Hardening Guidelines for Corporate Facilities Teams

The presentation provides enterprise defenders with network segmentation blueprints and firmware update practices for physical access infrastructure.

talks.title: Déjà Vu: Uncovering Stolen Open-Source Algorithms in Commercial Products
talks.teaser: Patrick Wardle and Tom McGuire expose commercial security vendors who covertly copied open-source macOS security tools into commercial enterprise products.
talks.summary:
The Ethics of Open-Source Security Software

Open-source security tools (such as Objective-See macOS utilities) are created for the public good, but commercial vendors often incorporate them without attribution or license compliance.

Discovering Code Plagiarism via Reverse Engineering

Patrick Wardle and Tom McGuire reverse engineer commercial macOS endpoint security products, identifying identical disassembled functions and decompiled logic.

Comparing Open-Source Engines with Commercial Binaries

The speakers present side-by-side binary diffing analysis demonstrating that proprietary endpoint agents directly lifted open-source behavioral monitoring engines.

Community Accountability and Legal Ramifications

The authors discuss intellectual property protection, GPL license enforcement, and building ethical accountability across the cybersecurity industry.

talks.title: The Big Rick: How I Rickrolled My High School District & Got Away With It
talks.teaser: High school student Minh Duong shares how he orchestrated a synchronized district-wide Rickroll across six high schools by exploiting networked IPTV projectors.
talks.summary:
The Setup: Networked Projectors and High School Curiosity

High school district networks often suffer from flat network topologies, default credentials, and unsegmented IoT devices accessible from student Wi-Fi.

Discovering Vulnerabilities in Networked Projectors and IPTV

Minh Duong demonstrates mapping district subnets, uncovering unauthenticated web interfaces, exposed Telnet ports, and universal broadcast APIs on classroom display devices.

Orchestrating the Synchronized Multi-School Rickroll

Duong explains writing automated Python scripts to synchronize video playback and volume control across hundreds of displays simultaneously right before the morning bell.

Responsible Disclosure and Administrative Reactions

The presentation highlights how Duong prepared a comprehensive 26-page vulnerability report, resulting in district-wide network hardening and praise from school administrators.

talks.title: Automotive Ethernet Fuzzing: Low-Cost Virtual Testbeds & Vulnerability Research
talks.teaser: Researchers from Hyundai AutoEver present a low-cost virtual testbed for automotive Ethernet, fuzzing SOME/IP and DoIP protocol stacks to find ECU vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
The Transition from CAN Bus to Automotive Ethernet

Modern connected and autonomous vehicles increasingly adopt Automotive Ethernet (100BASE-T1) to support high-bandwidth sensor telemetry and infotainment communications.

Challenges in Automotive Protocol Vulnerability Research

Jonghyuk Song, Soohwan Oh, and Woongjo Choi explain the financial and physical barriers to conducting vehicle security research on real automotive hardware.

Building a Low-Cost Virtual Automotive Ethernet Testbed

The researchers demonstrate developing a modular virtual test environment emulating SOME/IP, DoIP, and AVB communication stacks.

Automated Fuzzing and ECU Vulnerability Discovery

The authors share fuzzing methodology results, demonstrating zero-day crash discoveries across automotive gateway and head unit firmware implementations.

talks.title: Doing the Impossible: Finding Mainframe Buffer Overflows in z/OS
talks.teaser: Jake Labelle demystifies IBM z/OS mainframe security, demonstrating how to find and exploit memory corruption buffer overflows in legacy enterprise mainframes.
talks.summary:
The Critical and Overlooked World of Enterprise Mainframes

Mainframes process over 70% of global financial transactions and airline reservations, yet security auditing of IBM z/OS systems remains a rare and misunderstood discipline.

Understanding z/Architecture and High-Level Assembler (HLASM)

Jake Labelle breaks down mainframe memory layouts, 31-bit/64-bit addressing, Base-Displacement memory management, and HLASM calling conventions.

Discovering and Exploiting Mainframe Buffer Overflows

Labelle demonstrates finding memory corruption bugs in authorized system programs (APF-authorized libraries) and constructing custom payloads to seize Supervisor State.

Defensive Hardening for Mainframe Environments

The presentation provides enterprise security teams with auditing checklists, system integrity verification practices, and logging configurations for z/OS systems.

talks.title: You Have 1 New Appwntment: Hacking Proprietary iCalendar Properties
talks.teaser: Eugene Lim (spac3sc) explores vulnerabilities in the ubiquitous iCalendar (.ics) standard, demonstrating zero-click XSS, RCE, and credential theft via calendar invites.
talks.summary:
The Ubiquitous and Insecure iCalendar Standard

First standardized in 1998, the iCalendar (.ics) specification is universally supported by email clients, mobile operating systems, and enterprise scheduling software.

Auditing Proprietary Vendor Extensions and Parsers

Eugene Lim analyzes how major vendors implement custom, undocumented X-properties, leading to parsing inconsistencies and injection vulnerabilities.

Demonstrating Zero-Click Exploits via Calendar Invites

Lim showcases real-world exploit chains across popular email clients and web apps—triggering stored cross-site scripting (XSS), URL scheme handler hijacking, and remote code execution.

Hardening Calendar Ingestion Pipelines

The author outlines essential parsing sanitization standards, Content Security Policy adjustments, and safe calendar processing practices.

talks.title: The COW: Container on Windows Who Escaped the Silo
talks.teaser: Eran Segal investigates Windows container isolation (Process Isolation & Hyper-V), demonstrating novel container escape techniques via Silo IPC mechanisms.
talks.summary:
The Foundations of Windows Container Sandboxing

Windows Containers use Server Silos and Job Objects for process-isolated containers and lightweight Hyper-V VMs for hardware-enforced isolation.

Analyzing Windows Kernel Silo Architecture

Eran Segal explores how the NT kernel isolates named objects, registry hives, and file system namespaces between silos and the host OS.

Discovering IPC and Driver Boundary Escapes

Segal demonstrates exploiting unconstrained driver communication handles and shared system memory mappings to break out of Windows container silos.

Securing Multi-Tenant Windows Cloud Workloads

The author provides guidance on hardening Windows container hosts, configuring Hyper-V isolation boundaries, and monitoring kernel telemetry.

talks.title: Trailer Shouting: Talking PLC4TRUCKS Remotely with an SDR
talks.teaser: Ben Gardiner demonstrates using Software Defined Radios (SDR) to transmit and decode SAE J2497 (PLC4TRUCKS) signals over the air, spoofing heavy vehicle trailer brakes.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Power Line Communications in Heavy Trucks

Commercial tractor-trailers utilize the SAE J2497 (PLC4TRUCKS) protocol to communicate between tractor cab controllers and trailer Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) over DC power lines.

Unintended RF Emissions from Trailer Wiring

Ben Gardiner and team discover that high-frequency PLC signals radiate significantly from unshielded tractor-trailer power cables acting as broadcast antennas.

Over-the-Air Transmission and Packet Injection with SDRs

Gardiner demonstrates using low-cost SDR hardware to transmit J2497 FSK packets wirelessly, manipulating trailer ABS brake diagnostic commands from a distance.

Mitigations for Commercial Vehicle Fleets

The presentation discusses physical shielding, cryptographic protocol extensions, and testing guidelines for heavy vehicle cybersecurity.

talks.title: The Hitchhacker's Guide to iPhone Lightning & JTAG Hacking
talks.teaser: Thomas Roth (stacksmashing) reverses the proprietary Apple Lightning connector and Tristar chip, building open-source hardware to enable JTAG debugging on iPhones.
talks.summary:
The Hidden Capabilities of Apple's Lightning Connector

Beyond charging and data transfer, Apple's 8-pin Lightning connector contains proprietary multiplexing hardware used for factory diagnostics and low-level serial debugging.

Reverse Engineering the Tristar and Hydra ICs

Thomas Roth analyzes the serial handshake protocol (SDQ) used by the Lightning cable to negotiate multiplexed analog and digital pin assignments.

Building Custom Hardware for JTAG Multiplexing

Roth details designing open-source breakout hardware and firmware to command Tristar into exposing raw hardware JTAG and SWD debug ports.

Unlocking Low-Level Hardware Research on iOS Devices

The presentation provides security researchers with open-source schematics and firmware to inspect baseband and application processors on iPhones.

talks.title: Evil PLC Attacks: Weaponizing PLCs as Attack Platforms
talks.teaser: Sharon Brizinov demonstrates 'Evil PLC' attacks, weaponizing compromised industrial PLCs as offensive footholds to compromise engineering workstations.
talks.summary:
Flipping the Script on Industrial Control System Attacks

While traditional ICS attacks focus on compromising engineering workstations to attack PLCs, Sharon Brizinov explores weaponizing the PLC itself as a predatory platform.

Storing Offensive Payloads in PLC Logic and Memory

Brizinov demonstrates embedding malicious code and weaponized project files directly inside PLC controller memory.

Compromising Engineers During Routine Maintenance

When maintenance engineers connect engineering software (TIA Portal, RSLogix) to perform diagnostic downloads, the weaponized PLC exploits vulnerabilities in the engineering workstation.

Hardening Industrial Maintenance Workflows

The author provides defensive mitigations—including engineering software sandboxing, cryptographic project signing, and controller integrity verification.

talks.title: UFOs, Alien Life, and the Least Untruthful Things I Can Say
talks.teaser: Philosopher and cybersecurity veteran Richard Thieme explores four decades of government disclosure, intelligence culture, and epistemology in UFO/UAP research.
talks.summary:
Epistemology and Intelligence Culture

Richard Thieme draws on four decades of research into government intelligence institutions, examining how classified research paradigms interact with public perception.

The Mechanics of Strategic Deception and Plausible Deniability

Thieme analyzes the historical techniques used by intelligence agencies to manage sensitive technological developments and maintain secrecy.

Critical Thinking at the Boundaries of Human Knowledge

The speaker explores the cognitive biases, compartmentalization, and psychological dynamics that govern belief systems inside institutional research.

Lessons in Epistemic Humility for Hackers

The presentation challenges the hacker community to apply rigorous investigative skepticism to all forms of institutional narrative and data.

talks.title: Hack the Hemisphere: Uplinking to a Geostationary Satellite
talks.teaser: Karl Koscher and Andrew Green share how they legally acquired an uplink license to broadcast audio streams across the Western Hemisphere using an old satellite.
talks.summary:
An Unprecedented Satellite Research Opportunity

The Shadytel research cabal obtained legal FCC authorization to uplink signals to a vacant transponder slot on a decommissioning geostationary communications satellite.

Sourcing and Modifying Ground Station Hardware

Karl Koscher and Andrew Green detail sourcing surplus commercial dish antennas, feed horns, and high-power traveling-wave tube amplifiers (TWTAs).

Configuring DVB-S and SDR Transmission Chains

The speakers explain aligning the dish to the orbital slot, matching transponder frequency plans, and transmitting digital broadcast streams via open-source SDR tools.

Transcontinental RF Coverage and Lessons Learned

The authors present telemetry captures and broadcast reception logs spanning North America, sharing practical advice for satellite security research.

talks.title: OpenCola: The Anti-Social Network for Decentralized Collaboration
talks.teaser: John Midgley presents OpenCola, a peer-to-peer, privacy-first decentralized social and collaboration platform designed to eliminate centralized surveillance.
talks.summary:
The Surveillance Economy of Centralized Social Media

Modern social networking platforms profit by mining user personal data, behavioral tracking, and algorithmic manipulation of information feeds.

Architecting a True Peer-to-Peer Social Mesh

John Midgley introduces OpenCola, an open-source decentralized network that replaces centralized servers with local, peer-to-peer cryptographic nodes.

Cryptographic Identity and Gossip Protocol Synchronization

Midgley details using public-key cryptography for sovereign identity management and distributed hash tables (DHTs) for gossip-based feed dissemination.

Empowering Users with Data Sovereignty

The author discusses the user experience, search indexing capabilities, and cryptographic resilience of sovereign social systems.

talks.title: Analyzing PIPEDREAM: Challenges in Testing an ICS Attack Toolkit
talks.teaser: Dragos principal researcher Jimmy Wylie breaks down PIPEDREAM, a modular industrial attack toolkit developed by state-sponsored actors to disrupt industrial processes.
talks.summary:
The Emergence of PIPEDREAM (Cherovite) Malware

PIPEDREAM represents the seventh known ICS-specific malware platform, designed with modular capabilities to target widespread PLCs and industrial protocols.

Dissecting PIPEDREAM's Modular Architecture

Jimmy Wylie analyzes components targeting CODESYS, Modbus, OPC UA, and Omron PLCs, demonstrating its cross-vendor industrial attack capabilities.

Testing and Validating ICS Malware in Physical Testbeds

Wylie discusses the unique engineering challenges and safety risks of executing destructive industrial malware within physical hardware labs.

Detection Engineering and Threat Hunting in OT Networks

The author provides defensive OT monitoring recommendations, protocol anomaly heuristics, and asset inventory strategies to detect PIPEDREAM activity.

talks.title: Chromebook Breakout: Escaping Jail Using a Pico Ducky
talks.teaser: Jimi Allee demonstrates escaping enterprise-enrolled Chromebook kiosk mode using a Raspberry Pi Pico Ducky and living-off-the-land command injection.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Enterprise ChromeOS Enrollment

ChromeOS devices in educational and enterprise environments enforce strict management policies, disabling developer mode and restricting device usage to locked kiosk apps.

Building a Low-Cost Pico Ducky Hardware Tool

Jimi Allee shows how to program an affordable Raspberry Pi Pico running CircuitPython into a programmable BadUSB keystroke injection tool.

Chaining Diagnostic Shortcuts with Command Injection

Allee walks through an exploit chain exploiting debugging shortcuts, accessibility menus, and local command injection to spawn an unconstrained root shell.

Restoring Device Freedom and Enterprise Mitigations

The author explains how to un-enroll locked devices and provides ChromeOS administrators with policy configurations to patch kiosk breakout paths.

talks.title: Do Not Trust the ASA, Trojans: Implanting Cisco ASA Firewalls
talks.teaser: Jacob Baines demonstrates reverse engineering Cisco ASA firewalls, implanting persistent firmware backdoors, and subverting integrity verification checks.
talks.summary:
Cisco ASA as High-Value Perimeter Targets

Cisco Adaptive Security Appliances (ASA) guard corporate network perimeters, making them prime targets for state-sponsored persistence and espionage.

Reverse Engineering Cisco ASA OS and ROMMON Bootloaders

Jacob Baines analyzes the x86 64-bit Linux-based architecture of modern ASA software and its hardware integrity checking mechanisms.

Developing In-Memory and Persistent Firmware Implants

Baines demonstrates modifying firmware images, bypassing code-signing verifications, and hooking core packet processing functions to establish stealthy C2 channels.

Forensics and Verification Techniques for Network Defenders

The author shares forensic scripts and memory inspection methodologies to help network administrators detect backdoored ASA firewalls.

talks.title: All Roads Lead to GKE's Host: 4+ Ways to Escape Google Kubernetes Engine
talks.teaser: Billy Jheng and Muhammad Ramdhan demonstrate multiple novel container escape vectors in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) to achieve host node takeover.
talks.summary:
The Threat Model of Managed Kubernetes in the Cloud

In multi-tenant managed Kubernetes services like GKE, container boundaries must prevent untrusted workloads from escaping to underlying virtual machine nodes.

Analyzing GKE Node Agents and DaemonSets

Billy Jheng and Muhammad Ramdhan audit privileged background agents running on GKE nodes, discovering Unix socket exposure and shared host path mounts.

Four Novel Container Escape Attack Chains

The speakers walk through four distinct escape paths—exploiting containerd CRI bugs, fluentbit logging pipelines, metadata proxy bypasses, and kernel capabilities.

Remediation and Cloud Workload Hardening

The authors review Google's upstream security patches and demonstrate deploying GKE Sandbox (gVisor) and hardened node security profiles.

talks.title: Exploring Ancient Ruins to Find Modern Bugs: Auditing MS-RPC
talks.teaser: Akamai researchers Ben Barnea and Ophir Harpaz explore Microsoft Remote Procedure Call (MS-RPC), discovering zero-day vulnerabilities in core Windows services.
talks.summary:
The Ubiquitous and Complex World of MS-RPC

Microsoft Remote Procedure Call (MS-RPC) serves as the backbone communication protocol for nearly all internal Windows services, Domain Controllers, and enterprise servers.

Deconstructing RPC Interfaces, IDL, and NDR Engines

Ben Barnea and Ophir Harpaz dissect Network Data Representation (NDR) parsers and the complex type encoding mechanisms used across system services.

Discovering Zero-Days in Legacy RPC Handlers

The researchers demonstrate automated fuzzing and static analysis of undocumented RPC interfaces, uncovering critical memory corruption and privilege escalation bugs.

Hunting and Defending Against RPC-Based Exploitation

The authors release open-source RPC auditing tooling and provide detection engineers with RPC filter rules and telemetry hunting strategies.

talks.title: Tracking Military Ghost Helicopters Over Washington DC
talks.teaser: Andrew Logan investigates unattributed military and government helicopter flights over Washington D.C., tracking 'ghost' aircraft using crowdsourced ADS-B and acoustic data.
talks.summary:
The Mystery of Unattributed Helicopter Traffic in the Capital

Residents of Washington D.C. frequently report low-flying military and government helicopters, yet over 96% of official noise complaints go unattributed.

Crowdsourced ADS-B Telemetry and Transponder Inconsistencies

Andrew Logan analyzes crowdsourced ADS-B Exchange data, revealing aircraft operating with unassigned ICAO hex codes, delayed transponder pings, or disabled Mode-S.

Building Multi-Modal Acoustic and Visual Tracking Arrays

Logan details deploying a distributed network of acoustic microphones and automated sky-tracking cameras to identify aircraft types and flight paths in real time.

Transparency, Public Accountability, and Open-Source Intelligence

The presentation demonstrates the power of civilian OSINT in shedding light on unannounced military operations and government airspace usage.

talks.title: Reversing the Original Xbox Live Protocols: Reviving Online Gaming
talks.teaser: Tristan Miller reverses the original Xbox Live network protocols, explaining its proprietary Kerberos implementation and recreating open-source backend servers.
talks.summary:
The Legacy of the Original Xbox Live Network

Launched in 2002 and discontinued in 2010, the original Xbox Live service pioneered modern console online multiplayer using robust cryptographic hardware authentication.

Reverse Engineering Xbox Kerberos and Security Tokens

Tristan Miller dissects Xbox network packets, revealing how the console implemented a customized, encrypted variant of Kerberos v5 for ticketing and session key exchange.

Rebuilding the Backend: The Insignia Project

Miller details the engineering effort behind Insignia, an open-source cleanroom implementation of the Xbox Live server infrastructure.

Preserving Online Gaming History

The presentation showcases reviving authentic multiplayer matchmaking, friends lists, and voice chat for vintage consoles without modifying console hardware.

talks.title: How to Get MUMPS Thirty Years Later: Hacking the Government with FOIA'd Code
talks.teaser: Zachary Minneker explores MUMPS, a 1960s programming language powering the VA healthcare system, using FOIA-obtained source code to uncover critical vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
The Living Fossil of Healthcare Software: MUMPS

Developed in 1966 at Massachusetts General Hospital, MUMPS (M) remains the core operational language running major healthcare electronic record systems across the US government.

Acquiring Source Code via Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)

Zachary Minneker explains using FOIA requests to legally obtain thousands of lines of government VistA healthcare codebase routines.

Auditing Archaic Syntaxes and Database Routines

Minneker breaks down MUMPS global variables, dynamic code evaluation, and syntax quirks, uncovering severe injection vulnerabilities and authentication bypasses.

Modernizing and Securing Critical Government Healthcare IT

The author discusses the systemic challenges of auditing legacy national infrastructure and provides defensive isolation guidance.

talks.title: No-Code Malware: Windows 11 at Your Service via Power Automate
talks.teaser: Michael Bargury weaponizes Windows 11's built-in Power Automate for desktop, creating zero-binary, signatureless 'no-code malware' that bypasses EDR controls.
talks.summary:
The Pre-Installed Power Automate Engine in Windows 11

Windows 11 includes Power Automate for desktop out of the box, allowing users to automate desktop actions, keypresses, file transfers, and web requests.

Constructing Living-Off-The-Land No-Code Malware

Michael Bargury demonstrates building weaponized automation flows that perform credential harvesting, screen recording, and command execution using native signed Microsoft binaries.

Bypassing Modern EDR and Application Whitelisting

Because Power Automate executes flows via legitimate, trusted system processes, traditional EDR heuristics fail to detect malicious activity.

Enterprise Policy Controls and Flow Auditing

The presentation provides enterprise security administrators with group policy configurations to restrict Power Automate runtime and audit desktop flows.

talks.title: My First Hack Was in 1958: Reflections on Six Decades of Hacking
talks.teaser: Cybersecurity pioneer Winn Schwartau reflects on over six decades of hacker culture, from phone phreaking in 1958 to information warfare and future challenges.
talks.summary:
Six Decades of Hacker History

Winn Schwartau shares personal stories from the dawn of electronic exploration, beginning with audio oscillator experiments on analog phone lines in the late 1950s.

The Evolution of Information Warfare Concepts

Schwartau recounts introducing the concept of 'Electronic Pearl Harbor' to the US Congress in 1991 and predicting modern state-sponsored cyber operations.

The Shift from Technical Exploits to Cognitive Manipulation

The speaker explores the transition from hardware and software hacking to the weaponization of human psychology, social media, and reality perception.

Wisdom and Responsibility for Future Generations

The presentation encourages young security practitioners to preserve the curiosity, ethical integrity, and rebellious spirit of the original hacker community.

talks.title: Why Patients Should Hack Med Tech: Clinical Safety & Right to Repair
talks.teaser: Cory Doctorow, Dr. Christian Dameff, and Dr. Jeff Tully argue why patients and researchers must have the legal right to inspect and modify medical devices.
talks.summary:
The Monopolistic Lockdown of Medical Devices

Medical device manufacturers increasingly use digital rights management (DRM) and Section 1201 of the DMCA to lock down insulin pumps, pacemakers, and hospital ventilators.

The Flawed Argument of Proprietary Safety

Cory Doctorow, Dr. Christian Dameff, and Dr. Jeff Tully dismantle the claim that proprietary obscurity protects patient health, showing how unpatched bugs endanger lives.

Real-World Clinical Risks of Unauditable Systems

The physician-hackers present clinical case studies where vendor lock-in prevented rapid hospital maintenance and delayed critical medical updates.

Advocating for Medical Right-to-Repair and Research Exemption

The panel calls for comprehensive copyright reform and permanent DMCA exemptions for medical device security auditing and patient-driven modifications.

talks.title: Scaling the Security Researcher to Eliminate Open-Source Vulnerabilities
talks.teaser: Dan Kaminsky Fellow Jonathan Leitschuh shares automated bulk-remediation frameworks using CodeQL to fix thousands of vulnerabilities across open-source ecosystems.
talks.summary:
The Asymmetry of Open-Source Vulnerability Remediation

Every year, thousands of developer hours are spent discovering identical classes of known vulnerabilities (e.g. zip slips, temp file flaws) across disparate open-source repositories.

Automating Bulk Discovery with CodeQL

Jonathan Leitschuh demonstrates writing semantic CodeQL queries to identify structural security flaws across hundreds of thousands of public GitHub repositories.

Orchestrating Mass Pull Requests and Coordinated Fixes

Leitschuh explains building automated tooling (OpenRewrite, GitHub API scripts) to generate, submit, and track thousands of automated security pull requests.

Cultivating a Scalable Fix-First Security Paradigm

The author advocates for shifting security research incentives from purely publishing CVEs to building automated, ecosystem-wide remediation engines.

talks.title: Brazil Redux: Short-Circuiting Tech-Enabled Dystopia with Right to Repair
talks.teaser: Fight to Repair founder Paul Roberts analyzes corporate digital monopolies, anti-repair tactics, and the global legislative battle for the Right to Repair.
talks.summary:
The Dystopian Reality of Software-Locked Hardware

From smartphones and farm tractors to hospital equipment, manufacturers increasingly deploy cryptographic serializing and software locks to outlaw third-party repair.

Deconstructing Corporate Anti-Repair Arguments

Paul Roberts dismantles manufacturer claims that independent repair compromises user security and privacy, showing how DRM consolidates market monopolies.

Analyzing the Global Legislative and Regulatory Battle

Roberts reviews recent Right to Repair executive orders, FTC enforcement actions, and state legislation mandating parts and diagnostic tool availability.

The Crucial Role of the Hacker Community in Policy Reform

The presentation calls on reverse engineers and hardware hackers to provide technical evidence and expert testimony to lawmakers fighting for consumer repair rights.

talks.title: Moving Regulation Upstream: The Role of Digital Service Providers
talks.teaser: A panel of cyber policy experts discusses shifting regulatory burdens upstream to major digital service providers to protect organizations below the security poverty line.
talks.summary:
The Crisis of the Cyber Poverty Line

Small businesses, local governments, and hospitals struggle to achieve basic cyber resilience due to constrained financial budgets and severe cybersecurity staffing shortages.

Shifting the Burden: Moving Security Upstream

The panel explores why cybersecurity responsibilities must transition away from end-users and under-resourced organizations toward major cloud platforms and software vendors.

Regulatory Mandates and Secure-by-Design Standards

The speakers debate government policies, liability frameworks, and default security standards (e.g. mandatory multi-factor authentication, secure default configurations).

Architecting Collective Defense Across Digital Supply Chains

The discussion outlines strategic policy roadmaps for building resilient national cyber defense architectures.

talks.title: Emerging Technical Cyber Policy Topics: Bridging Hackers & Government
talks.teaser: Cyber policy practitioners discuss emerging legislative and national security policies affecting security research, encryption, and critical infrastructure defense.
talks.summary:
The Intersection of Technical Research and National Policy

As cyber threats directly impact critical infrastructure and international stability, government policymakers urgently require accurate technical guidance from the hacker community.

Key Policy Battlegrounds: Encryption, Disclosure, and Export Controls

The panel examines critical legislative debates—including client-side scanning proposals, mandatory vulnerability disclosure laws, and dual-use tool export restrictions.

Translating Technical Realities into Effective Legislation

The speakers analyze how ambiguous legal language in criminal statutes (CFAA) inadvertently chills vital defensive security research.

Actionable Pathways for Hacker Civic Engagement

The presentation provides researchers with concrete avenues for contributing expert testimony, public comments, and technical advisory to legislative bodies.

talks.title: Hacking Law is for Hackers: CFAA, DMCA, & Global Vulnerability Disclosure
talks.teaser: Legal experts Harley Geiger and DOJ's Leonard Bailey review landmark changes in hacker law, including Department of Justice CFAA policy revisions and DMCA reforms.
talks.summary:
A Landmark Year for Computer Crime Law

The 2021–2022 period brought historic legal developments reshaping the landscape for security researchers in the United States and internationally.

Analyzing the DOJ's New CFAA Charging Policy

Leonard Bailey details the US Department of Justice's policy shift explicitly declining to prosecute good-faith security researchers under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA).

DMCA Section 1201 Exemptions and Emerging Foreign Laws

Harley Geiger analyzes the latest triennial DMCA exemptions for security research and reviews new foreign vulnerability disclosure regulations (e.g., China's provisions).

Best Practices for Good-Faith Vulnerability Research

The speakers outline essential legal hygiene practices for researchers conducting audits, coordinated disclosures, and bug bounty engagements.

talks.title: Dragon Tails: Supply-Side Security & International Vulnerability Disclosure Law
talks.teaser: Atlantic Council researchers Stewart Scott and Trey Herr investigate global reliance on Chinese security research and the impact of China's mandatory disclosure laws.
talks.summary:
Global Software Reliance on Chinese Vulnerability Research

Western proprietary and open-source software ecosystems historically relied heavily on security vulnerabilities discovered and disclosed by Chinese researchers.

Analyzing China's 2021 Vulnerability Regulations

Stewart Scott and Trey Herr examine China's Provisions on the Management of Network Product Security Vulnerabilities, which mandate reporting zero-days to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) first.

Measuring the Supply-Side Shift in Zero-Day Disclosures

The researchers present quantitative data showing a steep drop in Chinese research contributions to international bug bounty platforms and Western CVE registries.

Geopolitical Consequences for Global Supply Chain Defense

The presentation evaluates policy responses for Western governments to foster domestic research talent and strengthen open-source software security.

talks.title: Tear Down This Zywall: Breaking Open Zyxel Encrypted Firmware
talks.teaser: Jay Lagorio demonstrates defeating proprietary encryption on Zyxel Zywall security gateway firmware, extracting executables to discover critical zero-days.
talks.summary:
The Barrier of Encrypted Embedded Firmware

Hardware manufacturers increasingly distribute encrypted firmware updates to thwart vulnerability research and protect proprietary software implementations.

Analyzing Zyxel's Encrypted Firmware Architecture

Jay Lagorio investigates the update packaging used across Zyxel Zywall enterprise firewalls, analyzing how decryption occurs inside device memory.

Extracting Hardware Keys and Emulating the Decryption Engine

Lagorio demonstrates dumping bootloader memory via hardware debug interfaces, extracting AES decryption keys, and building an automated firmware unpacker.

Uncovering Zero-Day Vulnerabilities in Unpacked Binaries

The author showcases discovering critical unauthenticated vulnerabilities in the decrypted web management daemon and shares remediation advice.

talks.title: Killer Hertz: Weapons-Grade RF Jamming & Electronic Counter-Measures
talks.teaser: Chris Rock investigates commercial and military Electronic Counter Measures (ECMs), demonstrating the physical and operational impacts of weapons-grade RF jammers.
talks.summary:
The Proliferation of High-Powered RF Jamming Systems

Governments, police agencies, and private entities deploy Electronic Counter Measures (ECMs) to jam cellular networks, drone frequencies, and satellite navigation.

Analyzing RF Power Amplification and Frequency Sweeping

Chris Rock explores the hardware mechanics of wideband barrage and sweep jammers, demonstrating output power calculations and heat dissipation challenges.

Operational Impacts on Emergency Services and Critical Infrastructure

Rock illustrates how rogue or poorly configured jammers blind cellular emergency services (E911), disrupt aircraft ADS-B telemetry, and disable security alarms.

Counter-Jamming Strategies and RF Triangulation

The presentation reviews directional antenna tracking, frequency hopping resilience, and regulatory enforcement tools used to locate illegal transmitters.

talks.title: Deanonymization of Tor HTTP Hidden Services via Timing & Header Side-Channels
talks.teaser: Ionut Cernica demonstrates novel side-channel attacks against Tor HTTP Onion Services, leaking the real backend IP address through HTTP header discrepancies.
talks.summary:
The Anonymity Model of Tor Onion Services

Tor Onion Services are designed to conceal the true IP address and geographic location of web servers, routing traffic through multi-hop rendezvous circuits.

Discovering Web Server Header and Timing Side-Channels

Ionut Cernica analyzes how default web server configurations (Apache, Nginx) leak backend network identifiers and clock skews.

Active Probing and IP Address Correlation Attacks

Cernica demonstrates crafting specialized HTTP requests that induce unique TCP responses, allowing an external observer to correlate the Onion service to a public IP.

Hardening Guidelines for Onion Service Operators

The author provides a comprehensive hardening blueprint—including custom error page sanitization, proxy stripping, and isolated virtualization.

talks.title: Walk This Way: What Run-DMC & Aerosmith Teach About the Future of Cybersecurity
talks.teaser: CISA Director Jen Easterly discusses the power of radical collaboration between government agencies and the hacker community, inspired by the 1986 Run-DMC/Aerosmith crossover.
talks.summary:
The Power of Unlikely Collaborations

Just as the 1986 crossover between Aerosmith and Run-D.M.C. revolutionized popular music, modern cybersecurity requires dismantling silos between government agencies and grassroots hackers.

Transforming CISA's Relationship with the Hacker Community

Jen Easterly outlines CISA's commitment to transparency, good-faith research protection, and active engagement with the DEF CON community.

Joint Cyber Defense Collaborative (JCDC) Initiatives

Easterly reviews operational achievements of public-private threat intelligence sharing during major critical vulnerability outbreaks (e.g. Log4j).

Building a Culture of Radical Transparency and Civic Defense

The presentation encourages hackers to collaborate directly with public defenders to secure critical infrastructure and democratic institutions.

talks.title: Let's Dance in the Cache: Destabilizing Hash Tables on Microsoft IIS
talks.teaser: Orange Tsai presents groundbreaking research into Microsoft IIS hash table implementations, weaponizing cache collisions and memory layout manipulation for RCE.
talks.summary:
The Fundamental Role of Hash Tables in Web Servers

Hash tables are ubiquitous data structures used by web servers like Microsoft IIS to manage request routing, module pipelines, and output caching.

Reverse Engineering Microsoft IIS Cache Internals

Orange Tsai analyzes the underlying hash algorithms and bucket resolution mechanisms inside the IIS core binary (http.sys and w3core.dll).

Inducing Deterministic Hash Collisions and Cache Confusion

Tsai demonstrates crafting specific URL requests to induce hash collisions, corrupting internal cache tables and overwriting cached authentication states.

Achieving Pre-Auth Remote Code Execution on Windows Servers

The author details weaponizing cache corruption to gain unauthorized remote code execution on fully patched Microsoft IIS servers.

talks.title: Hunting Bugs in the Tropics: Auditing Aruba Enterprise Networks
talks.teaser: Daniel Jensen details hunting for vulnerabilities across Aruba's on-premises network management and wireless controller appliances, uncovering pre-auth RCE.
talks.summary:
The Threat Surface of Enterprise Network Appliances

Aruba Networks produces central management appliances (AirWave, ClearPass, Mobility Controllers) that govern entire corporate wireless and wired infrastructures.

Reverse Engineering Proprietary Aruba Daemons

Daniel Jensen audits embedded Linux firmware, dissecting custom C/C++ daemons, Java web services, and internal communication protocols.

Discovering Pre-Authentication Remote Code Execution Flaws

Jensen demonstrates chaining unauthenticated protocol manipulation, deserialization flaws, and command injection to obtain root access on target controllers.

Remediation and Enterprise Network Hardening

The presentation provides network engineers with advice on isolating management interfaces and managing vendor firmware updates.

talks.title: A Dead Man's Full-Yet-Responsible-Disclosure System
talks.teaser: Yolan Romailler designs a cryptographic dead man's switch for vulnerability disclosure, using timelock encryption and witness networks to ensure ethical release.
talks.summary:
The Dilemma of Vulnerability Disclosure Timelines

Security researchers facing non-responsive vendors or hostile legal threats often lack guaranteed mechanisms to ensure vulnerabilities are addressed before disclosures become public.

Designing a Cryptographic Dead Man's Switch

Yolan Romailler introduces a protocol combining secret sharing, timelock puzzles, and decentralized witness networks to create an immutable disclosure countdown.

Automating Progressive and Responsible Key Release

Romailler demonstrates how researchers can pause, extend, or permanently abort the decryption process upon successful vendor patch verification.

Legal and Ethical Implications for Security Researchers

The author discusses the legal protections, game theory incentives, and ethical safeguards built into automated disclosure systems.

talks.title: The Internet's Role in Sanctions Enforcement: Russia, Ukraine, & The Future
talks.teaser: PCH executive director Bill Woodcock explores the role of global Internet routing and governance (ICANN, RIPE, BGP) in international sanctions enforcement during wartime.
talks.summary:
Wartime Petitions for Internet Isolation

Following the invasion of Ukraine, Ukrainian officials petitioned ICANN and RIPE NCC to revoke top-level domains (.ru) and block Russian IP prefix allocations.

Evaluating the Governance Architecture of the Global Internet

Bill Woodcock analyzes why internet governance bodies resisted disconnecting sovereign states, emphasizing the fundamental neutrality of root DNS and Regional Internet Registries (RIRs).

Technical Sanctions vs. BGP and Peering Realities

Woodcock breaks down how internet exchange points (IXPs), transit providers, and tier-1 carriers handle international sanctions without fragmenting global routing.

The Future of the Open, Global Internet in Geopolitical Conflicts

The presentation warns against the weaponization of core routing infrastructure and advocates for preserving universal digital communication.

talks.title: Wireless Keystroke Injection via Bluetooth Low Energy on Windows
talks.teaser: Jose Pico and Fernando Perera demonstrate exploiting Windows Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) pairing flaws to execute unauthorized wireless keystroke injection.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Bluetooth Low Energy Peripherals

Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) human interface devices (keyboards, mice, remotes) are widely paired with modern Windows workstations and laptops.

Discovering BLE Pairing State Machine Flaws in Windows

Jose Pico and Fernando Perera analyze Windows Bluetooth stack implementations, discovering vulnerabilities in device re-connection and authentication handshakes.

Impersonating Legitimate BLE Keyboards Over the Air

The researchers demonstrate spoofing authorized BLE MAC addresses and characteristics to inject arbitrary keystrokes at high speeds without user interaction.

Remediation and Bluetooth Endpoint Hardening

The authors review Microsoft's patch deployment (CVE-2022-21999) and offer enterprise guidelines for managing wireless Bluetooth peripherals.

talks.title: Hacking ISPs with Point-to-Pwn Protocol over Ethernet (PPPoE)
talks.teaser: Gal Zror turns the tables on SOHO router research, demonstrating how compromised customer routers exploit upstream ISP PPPoE concentrators and infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Reversing the Attack Vector: Router to ISP Infrastructure

While security research typically focuses on hacking consumer SOHO routers from the internet, Gal Zror explores attacking ISP core networks directly from compromised routers.

Analyzing Point-to-Point Protocol over Ethernet (PPPoE)

Zror investigates the PPPoE handshake protocol used by millions of broadband modems to establish authenticated WAN connections with ISP access concentrators (BRASS/BNG).

Fuzzing PPPoE Daemons and Kernel Parsers

The speaker demonstrates fuzzing proprietary and open-source PPPoE implementations, uncovering memory corruption and remote code execution vulnerabilities in ISP aggregation nodes.

Securing Broadband Access Networks

The presentation provides telecom network architects with guidance on protocol validation, process sandboxing, and subscriber isolation.

talks.title: Browser-Powered Desync Attacks: A New Frontier in HTTP Request Smuggling
talks.teaser: PortSwigger head of research James Kettle unveils browser-powered desync attacks, turning victim web browsers into desynchronization weapons against major websites.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of HTTP Request Smuggling

HTTP Request Smuggling historically required direct socket-level control to send malformed byte sequences between reverse proxies and backend servers.

Weaponizing Web Browsers for Desync Exploitation

James Kettle demonstrates how subtle protocol desynchronization bugs can be triggered directly from standard web browsers using JavaScript fetch and XMLHttpRequest.

Client-Side Desyncs and Request Hijacking

Kettle illustrates exploiting HTTP/1.1 pipeline reuse and HTTP/2 downgrade ambiguities to poison browser connection pools, hijack victim sessions, and steal credentials.

Hardening Next-Generation Web Architecture

The author provides open-source detection extensions (HTTP Request Smuggler) and actionable advice on end-to-end HTTP/2 enforcement.

talks.title: How Russia is Trying to Block Tor: Censorship & Pluggable Transports
talks.teaser: Tor Project co-founder Roger Dingledine analyzes Russia's nationwide Tor censorship apparatus (TSPU) and how pluggable transports fight back.
talks.summary:
The Escalation of Russian Internet Censorship

In late 2021 and early 2022, Russian authorities deployed Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) hardware (TSPU) across domestic ISPs to systematically block Tor.

Analyzing Censorship Vectors: IP Blacklists, TLS Probing, & DPI

Roger Dingledine dissects the multi-tiered blocking strategies used—including DNS poisoning, TLS client-hello fingerprinting, and active probing of directory authorities.

Deploying Pluggable Transports: Snowflake, obfs4, & WebTunnel

Dingledine demonstrates how modern circumvention protocols disguise Tor traffic as WebRTC video calls (Snowflake) or standard HTTPS web browsing.

The Cat-and-Mouse Game of Internet Freedom

The presentation emphasizes the importance of community bridge operators and open-source circumvention development in preserving access to uncensored information.

talks.title: Abusing Windows Error Reporting to Dump LSASS Memory
talks.teaser: Asaf Gilboa and Ron Ben-Yitzhak present a stealthy credential dumping technique that abuses native Windows Error Reporting (WER) to dump LSASS without alerts.
talks.summary:
The Heavy EDR Surveillance Around LSASS Access

Modern Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents strictly monitor `OpenProcess` and `MiniDumpWriteDump` calls targeting the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS).

Abusing Native Windows Error Reporting (WER) Mechanisms

Asaf Gilboa and Ron Ben-Yitzhak demonstrate manipulating legitimate system crash handling daemons (WerFault.exe) to generate LSASS memory dumps on demand.

Bypassing EDR Detections Without Exploiting Vulnerabilities

Because WerFault is a trusted, digitally signed operating system binary, its memory dumping activity bypasses standard behavioral heuristics.

Detection Strategies and WER Telemetry Auditing

The authors provide blue teams with detection logic to audit WerFault command-line flags and anomalous crash dump creation events.

talks.title: Hidden Attack Surface of OEM IoT Devices: Zero-Click RCE in Top Routers
talks.teaser: Octavio Gianatiempo and Octavio Galland audit top-selling consumer routers, discovering systemic OEM firmware vulnerabilities that enable zero-click remote RCE.
talks.summary:
The Fragmented World of OEM Firmware Supply Chains

Many consumer networking brands rebrand hardware and firmware from Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), propagating legacy vulnerabilities across dozens of distinct products.

Reverse Engineering Embedded Router Firmware

Octavio Gianatiempo and Octavio Galland audit best-selling SOHO routers, analyzing closed-source MIPS binaries, proprietary UPnP handlers, and web daemons.

Discovering Zero-Click Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities

The researchers demonstrate exploiting unauthenticated stack buffer overflows in network management daemons to gain root shell access remotely.

Securing the Embedded Device Ecosystem

The presentation discusses vendor disclosure challenges with white-label manufacturers and provides hardening recommendations for consumers and ISPs.

talks.title: Trace Me If You Can: Bypassing Linux Syscall Tracing
talks.teaser: Rex Guo and Junyuan Zeng present novel techniques that allow unprivileged user-mode Linux processes to execute hidden system calls, bypassing ptrace and auditd.
talks.summary:
The Reliance on System Call Tracing in Linux Security

Linux security monitors, sandboxes, and behavioral audit frameworks (ptrace, seccomp, auditd) rely on intercepting system calls to validate process behavior.

Uncovering Architecture and Signal Handling Flaws

Rex Guo and Junyuan Zeng analyze x86/x64 syscall entry points, vDSO mechanisms, and asynchronous signal handling inside the Linux kernel.

Executing Covert Syscalls Without Triggering Trace Hooks

The authors demonstrate reliable techniques where an unprivileged program executes arbitrary system calls while blinding audit hooks and trace monitors.

Kernel Hardening and Robust Syscall Interception

The presentation reviews proposed kernel patches and alternative tracing architectures (eBPF probes, LSM hooks) to ensure tamper-proof telemetry.

talks.title: Leak the Planet: Veritatem Cognoscere Non Pereat Mundus
talks.teaser: Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets) founders Emma Best and Xan North discuss the archiving, ethical curation, and investigative impact of public data leaks.
talks.summary:
The Proliferation of Massive Data Leaks

From misconfigured cloud buckets and hacktivist breaches to insider whistleblowers, public interest datasets are leaking at unprecedented volumes.

Archiving and Indexing Complex Datasets with DDoSecrets

Emma Best and Xan North explain the technical infrastructure required to securely ingest, verify, sanitize, and index terabytes of leaked materials for journalists.

Ethical Curation and Balancing Public Interest vs. Privacy

The speakers explore the rigorous ethical protocols used to redact sensitive personal data, medical records, and PII before public indexing.

The Vital Role of Leaks in Investigative Accountability

The presentation highlights major investigations enabled by leak archives and advocates for secure, independent archiving infrastructure.

talks.title: Phreaking 2.0: Abusing Microsoft Teams Direct Routing
talks.teaser: Moritz Abrell demonstrates modern VoIP phreaking against Microsoft Teams Direct Routing, exploiting SIP and Session Border Controller (SBC) misconfigurations.
talks.summary:
The Integration of PSTN and Enterprise Cloud Communications

Microsoft Teams Direct Routing allows organizations to connect their on-premises telephony infrastructure and Session Border Controllers (SBCs) to Teams cloud.

Auditing Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) Handshakes

Moritz Abrell analyzes the SIP signaling and TLS mutual authentication used between enterprise SBCs and Microsoft cloud servers.

Exploiting Routing Misconfigurations for Toll Fraud and Interception

Abrell demonstrates spoofing caller IDs, bypassing trunk authorization rules, making unmetered international calls, and intercepting enterprise voice channels.

Hardening Enterprise SIP and Teams Telephony

The author provides VoIP administrators with SBC hardening checklists, strict TLS certificate validation rules, and SIP firewall configurations.

talks.title: Process Injection: Breaking All macOS Security Layers with a Single Vulnerability
talks.teaser: Thijs Alkemade reveals how a single process injection vulnerability in macOS broke code signing, sandboxing, and Transparency Consent and Control (TCC).
talks.summary:
The Multi-Layered macOS Security Architecture

Modern macOS enforces strict security boundaries—including code signing, App Sandbox isolation, Hardened Runtime, and TCC privacy permissions.

Discovering Logic Flaws in Dynamic Linker Environment Handling

Thijs Alkemade investigates how specific system applications handled dynamic library loading and environment variables without proper validation.

Bypassing Sandboxes and Stealing TCC Permissions

Alkemade demonstrates injecting arbitrary dynamic libraries into privileged Apple applications, inheriting their full entitlement set and accessing cameras and microphones.

Apple Remediation and macOS Hardening Lessons

The author reviews Apple's security patches and discusses the broader implications for hardened runtime design in desktop operating systems.

talks.title: Space Jam: Exploring Radio Frequency Attacks in Outer Space
talks.teaser: Dr. James Pavur investigates physical and protocol-level RF vulnerabilities in satellite constellations, demonstrating jamming, spoofing, and eavesdropping risks.
talks.summary:
The Fragile Radio Dependency of Space Systems

Every satellite mission—from low-Earth orbit broadband constellations to geostationary communications—relies on long-distance, unshielded RF links.
