Analyzing Satellite Uplink, Downlink, & Inter-Satellite Links

Dr. James Pavur breaks down the RF architectures of modern satellites, assessing vulnerabilities to ground-based jamming, signal interception, and spoofing.

Simulating Real-World Electronic Attacks on Orbiting Payloads

Pavur demonstrates how low-power transmitters on the Earth's surface can degrade satellite receivers and hijack unauthenticated telemetry channels.

Architecting Resilient Space Communications

The presentation provides aerospace engineers with concrete cryptographic hardening patterns, beam-steering mitigations, and protocol integrity standards.

talks.title: Weaponizing Windows Syscalls: Pure Syscall Shellcode & Advanced Evasion
talks.teaser: Tarek Abdelmotaleb and Dr. Bramwell Brizendine demonstrate weaponizing Windows syscalls into pure position-independent shellcode, evading modern EDR hooks.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of User-Mode Hooking and EDR Monitoring

Modern Endpoint Detection and Response tools place inline API hooks in user-mode DLLs (ntdll.dll, kernel32.dll) to intercept malicious API calls.

Developing Pure Syscall-Based Shellcode

Tarek Abdelmotaleb and Dr. Bramwell Brizendine present a methodology for writing pure position-independent shellcode that invokes direct system calls natively.

Resolving Dynamic Syscall Numbers Across Windows Builds

The researchers explain techniques for dynamically resolving System Service Numbers (SSNs) across diverse Windows OS versions without calling hooked APIs.

Kernel-Level Defensive Telemetry and Detection

The authors discuss defensive telemetry mechanisms—including kernel-mode ETW Threat Intelligence (ETW-TI) and memory scanning—to detect direct syscall abuse.

talks.title: A Policy Fireside Chat with Jason Healey
talks.teaser: Cyber conflict historian Jason Healey reflects on the evolution of cybersecurity from the 1970s to modern national policy, sharing lessons for researchers.
talks.summary:
The Early History of Computer Security and Policy

Jason Healey (w0nk) looks back at the foundational decades of cybersecurity in the 1970s and 1980s, tracing the emergence of national computer emergency response teams.

The Dynamics of State-Sponsored Cyber Conflict

Healey explores the escalation of international cyber conflict and how defensive capabilities have struggled to maintain pace with state-sponsored offense.

The Vital Role of Independent Security Researchers

The speaker emphasizes the essential contribution of the hacker community in identifying systemic risks and holding corporate and government institutions accountable.

Strategic Policy Frameworks for the Future

The fireside chat explores policy recommendations for improving internet resilience, software liability, and collaborative defense.

talks.title: You're Muted, Rooted: Exploiting Zoom on macOS
talks.teaser: macOS security expert Patrick Wardle exposes a local privilege escalation zero-day in Zoom for macOS, gaining root privileges by subverting the auto-updater.
talks.summary:
The Security Posture of Ubiquitous Video Conferencing

Zoom is deployed across millions of corporate and personal devices, running privileged background updater daemons that make it a critical attack target.

Reverse Engineering the Zoom macOS Auto-Updater

Patrick Wardle dissects Zoom's privileged helper tool, analyzing how it verifies cryptographic signatures on incoming application update packages.

Exploiting Signature Verification Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU)

Wardle demonstrates bypassing signature verification via a race condition, tricking the privileged updater daemon into executing arbitrary root payloads.

Coordinated Disclosure and macOS Software Hardening

The author details the disclosure process with Zoom, the release of emergency patches, and best practices for secure privileged helper tool development.

talks.title: Backdooring Pickles: A Decade Later and Things Only Got Worse
talks.teaser: ColdwaterQ demonstrates backdooring Python pickle files in machine learning models, weaponizing PyTorch and TensorFlow weights for silent remote code execution.
talks.summary:
The Inherent Insecurity of Python Object Pickling

Python's pickle serialization format allows arbitrary code execution by design through the `__reduce__` method, a risk known for over a decade.

The Dangerous Intersection of Pickles and Machine Learning

ColdwaterQ reveals that modern AI/ML frameworks (PyTorch, Hugging Face, scikit-learn) routinely distribute model weights serialized as raw pickle files.

Crafting Stealthy Backdoored AI Models

The researcher demonstrates weaponizing popular pre-trained models on public repositories to execute reverse shells when loaded by data scientists.

Moving Toward Safe AI Model Serialization Formats

The author advocates for transitioning the AI industry to safe serialization formats like Safetensors and demonstrates automated pickle auditing tools.

talks.title: Emoji Shellcoding: 🛠️, 🧌, and 🤯
talks.teaser: Hadrien Barral demonstrates crafting fully functional executable shellcode consisting entirely of valid multi-byte UTF-8 emoji characters.
talks.summary:
The Art of Constrained Shellcode Development

Exploit developers frequently encounter restrictive character filters (alphanumeric, ASCII, uppercase) that eliminate traditional byte sequences.

Deconstructing UTF-8 Encoding and Emoji Byte Spaces

Hadrien Barral explores the 4-byte UTF-8 encoding space used by modern emoji characters, mapping valid emoji bytes to x86 and ARM instruction opcodes.

Synthesizing Valid Instructions and Register Setup

Barral demonstrates assembling self-modifying decoder loops and setting up register arguments using only valid emoji sequences.

Implications for Deep Packet Inspection and Filter Evasion

The presentation illustrates how emoji-encoded payloads slip past text filters, chat sanitizers, and signature-based intrusion detection systems.

talks.title: Global Challenges, Global Approaches in Cyber Policy
talks.teaser: International cyber policy leaders discuss shared global challenges in software supply chain integrity, common vulnerability management, and multilateral defense.
talks.summary:
Common Threats in a Borderless Digital Domain

While nation-states maintain distinct domestic legal frameworks, they face identical cyber adversaries, vulnerable open-source dependencies, and interconnected digital supply chains.

Evaluating Multilateral Cybersecurity Agreements

The panel examines international policy initiatives—including the Paris Call, UN Open-Ended Working Group (OEWG), and bilateral ransomware task forces.

Managing Supply Chain Vulnerabilities Across Borders

The speakers debate coordinated global approaches to Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs), secure development standards, and cloud provider regulation.

Building Resilient Global Defense Alliances

The discussion emphasizes the necessity of cross-border operational cooperation between CERTs, researchers, and public infrastructure operators.

talks.title: One Bootloader to Load Them All: Subverting UEFI Secure Boot
talks.teaser: Mickey Shkatov and Jesse Michael expose vulnerabilities in signed UEFI third-party bootloaders, demonstrating complete Secure Boot bypass across millions of PCs.
talks.summary:
The Foundation of UEFI Secure Boot

Secure Boot verifies the cryptographic signatures of all boot stages—from UEFI firmware to OS bootloaders—against Microsoft-trusted keys stored in NVRAM.

Auditing the Microsoft 3rd Party UEFI Certificate Ecosystem

Mickey Shkatov and Jesse Michael investigate dozens of OEM, enterprise rescue, and dual-boot bootloaders signed by Microsoft's Third-Party UEFI CA.

Exploiting Bootloader Vulnerabilities to Execute Untrusted Code

The researchers demonstrate weaponizing memory corruption and unvalidated configuration execution in signed bootloaders to bypass Secure Boot entirely.

Managing the Revocation Crisis and Firmware Patching

The authors analyze the complex challenges of managing UEFI Secure Boot Forbidden Signature Database (DBX) revocation lists across legacy hardware.

talks.title: Avoiding Memory Scanners: Customizing Malware to Evade YARA & PE-sieve
talks.teaser: Kyle Avery presents techniques for evading in-memory scanners (PE-sieve, Moneta, YARA), demonstrating advanced sleep obfuscation and heap encryption.
talks.summary:
The Rise of In-Memory Threat Hunting

Modern defensive tooling (PE-sieve, Moneta, memory YARA rules) inspects process memory at runtime to detect unbacked executable pages, hooked functions, and injected beacons.

Deconstructing In-Memory Artifacts and Detections

Kyle Avery analyzes what makes injected payloads detectable—including RWX memory page permissions, modified thread call stacks, and unencrypted in-memory strings.

Implementing Advanced Sleep Obfuscation and Memory Masking

Avery demonstrates implementing sleep masking techniques (Ekko, Foliage) that dynamically encrypt memory pages, strip executable permissions, and spoof call stacks during sleep cycles.

Evolving Blue Team Memory Forensics

The author provides incident responders with methodologies for catching sleep-obfuscated payloads via timer queue inspection and thread pool analysis.

talks.title: A Black-Box Security Evaluation of the SpaceX Starlink User Terminal
talks.teaser: KU Leuven researcher Lennert Wouters demonstrates a custom hardware modchip that executes voltage fault injection on the SpaceX Starlink user terminal to bypass secure boot.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of SpaceX Starlink User Terminals (Dishy)

The Starlink User Terminal (UT) relies on a custom quad-core ARM Cortex-A53 SoC with hardware-enforced verified boot to protect satellite network keys.

Black-Box Hardware Reverse Engineering

Lennert Wouters details tearing down the terminal PCB, decapping shielding, and analyzing power distribution networks and flash memory lines.

Executing Voltage Fault Injection (Glitching)

Wouters demonstrates building a low-cost custom modchip that injects precise voltage glitches into the eMMC and SoC power rails during bootrom execution.

Bypassing Secure Boot to Execute Custom Firmware

The author successfully bypasses bootrom signature verification, obtains root access, and explores Starlink backend satellite communication protocols.

talks.title: Running Rootkits Like a Nation-State Hacker: Subverting Driver Signing Enforcement
talks.teaser: Omri Misgav investigates Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attacks, subverting Windows Driver Signature Enforcement to deploy stealthy kernel rootkits.
talks.summary:
The Defense Model of Windows Kernel Code Integrity

On 64-bit Windows systems, Driver Signature Enforcement (DSE) mandates that all kernel-mode code be digitally signed with an extended validation certificate approved by Microsoft.

The BYOVD Technique: Weaponizing Signed Vulnerable Drivers

Omri Misgav analyzes how threat actors leverage legitimately signed but vulnerable commercial drivers to gain arbitrary kernel read/write primitives.

Disabling DSE and Unhooking Kernel Callbacks

Misgav demonstrates patching kernel variables (`g_CiOptions`), blinding EDR kernel callbacks, and executing unsigned nation-state rootkit payloads in Ring 0.

Defensive Solutions: Vulnerable Driver Blocklists & HVCI

The presentation details implementing Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity (HVCI) and automated vulnerable driver blocklisting to protect enterprise endpoints.

talks.title: A Policy Fireside Chat with the National Cyber Director
talks.teaser: National Cyber Director Chris Inglis joins journalist Kim Zetter for a fireside chat on the National Cybersecurity Strategy and public-private defense partnerships.
talks.summary:

talks.title: The PACMAN Attack: Breaking Pointer Authentication on Apple M1 with Hardware Attacks
talks.teaser: MIT researcher Joseph Ravichandran presents PACMAN, combining speculative execution side-channels with software bugs to brute-force Apple M1 pointer authentication.
talks.summary:
The Role of Pointer Authentication (PAC) on Apple Silicon

ARM Pointer Authentication (PAC) uses cryptographic signatures on memory pointers to detect and prevent memory corruption and control-flow hijacking attacks.

Merging Microarchitectural Side Channels with Software Exploitation

Joseph Ravichandran presents PACMAN, a novel attack methodology that uses speculative execution to leak PAC authentication results without crashing the target process.

Brute-Forcing Cryptographic PAC Signatures Silently

Ravichandran demonstrates using cache side channels (Prime+Probe) to guess valid pointer signatures across kernel and user space memory.

Implications for Hardware Security Architecture

The author discusses why software mitigations cannot fully fix hardware microarchitectural leaks and proposes next-generation CPU design improvements.

talks.title: OopsSec: The Bad, the Worst, and the Ugly of APT Operations Security
talks.teaser: SafeBreach research director Tomer Bar exposes hilarious and critical operational security blunders made by state-sponsored Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) groups.
talks.summary:
The Fallibility of Advanced Threat Actors

While state-sponsored APT groups possess sophisticated zero-days and massive budgets, their human operators frequently make catastrophic operational security (OPSEC) mistakes.

Analyzing Real-World Nation-State Blunders

Tomer Bar reviews case studies involving Iranian, Russian, and North Korean threat groups leaking internal development logs and leaving debugging symbols in production malware.

Tracking Developer Identity Leaks and Infrastructure Reuse

Bar demonstrates how reusing test domain names, personal email accounts, and staging GitHub repos enabled analysts to unmask threat actor identities.

Operationalizing Adversary OPSEC Failures for Threat Hunting

The presentation provides threat intelligence analysts with methodologies for hunting developer artifacts and tracking threat actor infrastructure pivots.

talks.title: Computer Hacks in the Russia-Ukraine War: Cyber Operations on the Modern Battlefield
talks.teaser: Kenneth Geers analyzes cyber operations in the Russia-Ukraine war, dissecting destructive wiper malware, Viasat satellite outages, and hacktivist mobilization.
talks.summary:
The First True Peer-to-Peer Cyber Conflict

The Russia-Ukraine war represents the most intense, multi-dimensional cyber conflict in history, integrating digital strikes with conventional kinetic warfare.

Dissecting Destructive Wiper Malware Families

Kenneth Geers analyzes the wave of destructive wipers deployed against Ukrainian infrastructure (HermeticWiper, CaddyWiper, Industroyer2) targeting government and financial data.

The Strategic Impact of the Viasat Satellite Attack

Geers details the Russian cyber attack on the KA-SAT satellite network, which severed military communications across Ukraine and impacted European infrastructure.

The Mobilization of the IT Army and Civilian Hacktivism

The author explores the unprecedented crowdsourcing of cyber defense, civilian DDoS mobilization, and the future doctrine of cyber warfare.

talks.title: Old Malware, New Tools: Analyzing Commodore 64 Viruses with Ghidra
talks.teaser: Cesare Pizzi uses NSA Ghidra and custom 6502 plugins to reverse engineer vintage Commodore 64 malware, uncovering surprising polymorphic complexity.
talks.summary:
The Historical Architecture of 8-Bit Malware

In the 1980s and 1990s, early virus writers developed ingenious, ultra-compact malicious code operating under severe memory constraints (64 KB RAM).

Configuring Ghidra for MOS 6502 Architecture

Cesare Pizzi demonstrates setting up custom Ghidra processor modules and loader plugins to analyze Commodore 64 disk images (D64) and PRG binaries.

Dissecting Vintage Polymorphic and Stealth Viruses

Pizzi walks through reverse engineering classic 8-bit malware, analyzing disk drive controller hooking, interrupt hijacking, and memory-resident stealth techniques.

Timeless Lessons in Reverse Engineering

The author shows how analyzing constrained retro architectures sharpens modern binary analysis intuition and reverse engineering skills.

talks.title: The DEF CON Policy Department: What We Are Trying to Do for Hackers in PolicyWorld
talks.teaser: The DEF CON Policy Department outlines its mission to represent the hacker community in Washington D.C., protecting good-faith security research and privacy rights.
talks.summary:
The Mission of the DEF CON Policy Department

As cybersecurity becomes central to national security, economic stability, and civil liberties, hackers need dedicated representation in the corridors of policy making.

Advocating for Good-Faith Research Protections

The team reviews legislative efforts to reform the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA), secure permanent DMCA exemptions, and establish safe harbors for vulnerability disclosure.

Educating Lawmakers on Cryptography and Technical Realities

The speakers describe ongoing engagements with congressional committees and regulatory bodies, providing technical clarity on encryption backdoors and client-side scanning.

How the DEF CON Community Can Get Involved

The presentation invites security researchers, engineers, and academics to contribute to policy briefs, public comments, and grassroots advocacy campaigns.

talks.title: The Journey From an Isolated Container to Cluster Admin in Service Fabric (Encore)
talks.teaser: Aviv Sasson presents the complete technical breakdown of FabricEscape (CVE-2022-30137), breaking out of Linux containers to seize full Azure Service Fabric cluster control.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Microsoft Service Fabric Clusters

Microsoft Service Fabric serves as a critical distributed container orchestration platform hosting core internal services across Microsoft Azure data centers.

Deconstructing the FabricEscape Exploit Mechanics

Aviv Sasson walks through the technical discovery of unvalidated symbolic link traversals and race conditions within the container lifecycle management daemon.

Escalating from Low-Privilege Container to Full Host and Node Admin

Sasson demonstrates weaponizing the flaw to break out of Linux container sandboxes, execute code on host nodes, and harvest cluster management certificates.

Remediation and Multi-Tenant Security Best Practices

The author discusses the coordinated vulnerability disclosure timeline and security engineering takeaways for cloud container orchestrators.

talks.title: Pulling Passwords out of Configuration Manager
talks.teaser: Christopher Panayi demonstrates exploiting Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager (MECM/SCCM) OS deployment mechanisms and network booting to extract enterprise Active Directory credentials.
talks.summary:
Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager in the Enterprise

Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager (MECM/SCCM) is ubiquitous across corporate networks, managing automated operating system deployments and administrative workflows for thousands of workstations and servers.

Exploiting Network Boot and OS Deployment Workflows

Christopher Panayi details how PXE booting and task sequence executions expose sensitive domain credentials across enterprise networks during client provisioning.

Extracting Active Directory Credentials

Panayi explores common MECM architecture misconfigurations—including unencrypted network shares, weakly protected media, and cleartext task sequence variables—that allow unauthenticated attackers to harvest elevated domain credentials.

Defensive Hardening and Mitigation Guidance

The presentation concludes with detection strategies and remediation guidance, demonstrating how administrators can secure task sequence variables and enforce network-level authentication across deployment points.
